subject: MAP: Benchmarking playbook & delivery sprint
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Erin Blake <erin@dataco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-22T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: Benchmarking playbook & delivery sprint

Hi Erin —

Thanks again for carving out time to align on the MAP. Attached is a first-pass benchmarking playbook (redwood_map_benchmark_plan_v1.pdf). The document lays out:

- Test objectives: TTFT (time-to-first-token), sustained throughput, p50/p95 latency, and targeted concurrency shapes.
- Acceptance criteria for the pilot (see Section 2).
- Test harness and account access needs.
- Proposed 4-day load window options next week.

Quick asks for your team:
- Confirm which environment we should target (staging vs. pre-prod) and the test accounts we can use.
- Approve the proposed windows below or suggest alternates.

Proposed windows (PST):
- Option A: Tue 26 May 10:00–14:00 (ramp + 2 sustained hours)
- Option B: Thu 28 May 20:00–00:00 (off-peak, louder concurrency)

Access notes: we need one test API key (scoped to read-only/eval) and a temporary runner account (user@test.dataco.com) so our load runner can authenticate. If you prefer, we can use our private VPC peering — either way we'll provide an access checklist.

Cc'ing Rishi and Marissa to confirm the test harness details and to take ownership of the execution.

Cheers,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
(415) 555-0124

Attachment: redwood_map_benchmark_plan_v1.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Erin Blake <erin@dataco.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: product_ops@dataco.com
Date: 2026-05-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Benchmarking playbook & delivery sprint

Laura —

Thanks for the doc. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- Environment: Please run initially against our staging cluster (staging.dataco.internal) — we'll open a temporary test subdomain and provide an API key.
- KPIs: For us the non-negotiables are TTFT < 250ms at p50 and p95 < 800ms at the target concurrency. Throughput target is ~1,200 tokens/sec sustained for the chat workload.
- Windows: Option B looks better for us (off-peak). We can also do a short validation run on Tue morning if you want to sanity-check connectivity.

I attached the sample production profile (dataco_sample_profile.csv) that represents our typical request distributions — please ensure the runner can simulate the mix.

I'll work with product_ops to generate the test key and will share it via our secure vault (IAM ticket will reference this thread).

—Erin
Erin Blake
Director, Platform & Integrations
DataCo Analytics
erin@dataco.com

Attachment: dataco_sample_profile.csv (CSV, 34KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Erin Blake <erin@dataco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-23T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Benchmarking playbook & delivery sprint

Erin / Laura —

We reviewed the profile and updated the playbook with a runner plan. Key operational notes:

- Runner: We'll deploy our load runner from a small fleet (4 instances) in us-west-2 to match your staging region.
- Concurrency shapes: ramp 0→600 users over 15 minutes, hold 90 minutes at 600 (chat threads multiplexed), then ramp to 1,200 for a 30-minute spike.
- Measurement: TTFT measured from request accept to first byte. We'll capture token throughput with per-second granularity and end-to-end latency including model forward time and queuing.
- Failover: If the staging endpoint fails to respond, the run will gracefully stop and we will collect logs for root cause.

I've attached the core load script we will run (load_script.sh) and an updated checklist. Marissa will lead result collection and post-run analysis.

Rishi
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Attachment: load_script.sh (shell script, 8KB)

From: product_ops@dataco.com
To: Erin Blake <erin@dataco.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-26T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Benchmarking playbook & delivery sprint

Erin here from product ops (forwarding for visibility).

We provisioned the staging subdomain and created a temporary API key scoped to the test runner (expires 2026-06-05). Key id: dc-test-2026-58 (we'll paste the cipher in the vault).

Constraints to note:
- No persistent caching on staging — results may differ from prod by ~8–12% for throughput.
- Token limits per minute are enforced at 180k tokens/min on staging. The runner should throttle when approaching that limit.

We're good for Option B (Thu 28 May 20:00–00:00 PST) and can allow a 30-minute connectivity check on Tue 26 May at 10:00 PST.

--product_ops@dataco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Thanks — quick operational notes after the smoke run tonight:

- Connectivity: pass (latency baseline 40–60ms to staging endpoint).
- Small config tweak: increased runner concurrency bucket size to avoid token-throttling artifacts.
- Data collection: logs are being uploaded to the shared Drive folder (link in MAP).

- Friday 29 May 10:00 PST: Preliminary results review (30 minutes).
- Monday 01 Jun: Final MAP deliverable (includes benchmark_results_summary.xlsx and recommended config changes).

Marissa

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Erin Blake <erin@dataco.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-02T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Benchmarking playbook & delivery sprint — results & close

Erin —

Thanks for working through the MAP with us. Per the agreed timeline, attached is the summary workbook (benchmark_results_summary.xlsx) and a short pass/fail verdict against your acceptance thresholds. Key highlights:

- TTFT: p50 = 180ms, p95 = 430ms (PASS vs. your TTFT < 250ms p50 and p95 < 800ms).
- Sustained throughput: measured 1,150 tokens/sec over 90 minutes at 600 concurrent sessions (within ~4% of your 1,200 target).
- Spike behavior: at 1,200 concurrent sessions we saw p95 increase to ~920ms (degraded — we observed queueing at the request broker).
- Recommendations: enable per-route batching controls and increase instance parallelism for spikes; we estimate a ~12% infra uplift to meet 1,200 tokens/sec sustained with <800ms p95 in peak.

Action items in the MAP (finalized):
- Redwood: provide a config patch and estimated cost delta for the uplift (Rishi, due Thu 04 Jun).
- DataCo: confirm whether you want to accept the uplift and proceed with Dedicated capacity trial (Erin, reply by Mon 07 Jun).
- Both: schedule a follow-up run if DataCo opts into the uplift.

If you want, we can convert the workbook into a short slide pack for your execs.

Best,
Laura

Attachment: benchmark_results_summary.xlsx (XLSX, 220KB)
